profile.reading: This is the Unipol data center in the Pilastro district of Bologna, Italy, developed for UnipolSai Assicurazioni by Consorzio Maestrale, with design work by Ariatta on mechanical, electrical and commissioning, Starching srl on architecture, and Redesco on structural engineering, moving from design in 2014 to completion in 2015. The facility comprises about 1,200 square meters, or roughly 12,900 square feet, of rack and server room space alongside about 1,600 square meters, or roughly 17,200 square feet, of office space, together totaling around 2,800 square meters, or roughly 30,100 square feet. It holds Uptime Institute Tier IV certification both for its design documents and as a constructed facility, though no public source discloses a specific power capacity figure in megawatts for the site, an honest gap this registry records rather than estimates. Unipol was founded in 1962 in Bologna as a cooperative non-life insurer and is today headquartered at the Unipol Tower in that same city, operating as a financial services holding company spanning insurance and banking through brands including UnipolSai, Linear Assicurazioni, Linear Life, UniSalute, and Arca Vita; in December 2024 UnipolSai was merged into its parent company, which was renamed Unipol Assicurazioni. For fiscal year 2024 the group reported total assets of about 83.4 billion euros, net income of about 1.1 billion euros, and roughly 12,000 employees, ranking among Italys largest insurers, though Generali holds the top spot nationally by premium volume rather than Unipol. The Pilastro building sits within Bolognas established technology and business district on the citys eastern edge, chosen by UnipolSai as a purpose built, insurer-owned facility rather than third party colocation space, reflecting the scale of an insurance group large enough to operate its own Tier IV certified core data center rather than relying solely on external cloud or colocation providers.
